extracted.intended_audience: practitioners before the USPTO (patent attorneys/agents and trademark practitioners), OED staff, and the legal/regulatory community interested in disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedure and standards for imposing reciprocal discipline by the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including notice/service requirements, grounds for opposition, consequences of failing to respond, and the form of discipline (public reprimand) and publication requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline upon a practitioner that is identical to discipline imposed by a duly constituted state authority pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may order discipline identical to the state-imposed discipline (here: public reprimand) and take action pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24. The Final Order here imposes a public reprimand identical to the State Bar Court of California's public reproval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and service requirements (Notice and Order; certified mail; delivery)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' must be mailed (here by certified mail with receipt) and delivered to the respondent. The Notice and Order provided an opportunity to file a response within forty (40) days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of mailing/delivery (e.g., certified mail receipt number) is part of the record. The Notice delivered on January 12, 2018, and specified the 40-day response window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible grounds to oppose reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may file a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to the state discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order references the regulatory grounds (11.24(d)(1)) but does not list them; respondents should consult that provision for specific defenses (e.g., lack of jurisdiction, procedural defects, differing misconduct).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to respond (no genuine issue of material fact)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response to the Notice and Order within the allotted period, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and proceed to impose the reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case, because Respondent did not file a response, the Director determined no genuine issue of material fact existed and ordered public reprimand as appropriate discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct defined by 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) (public discipline by a state)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) states that it is misconduct for a practitioner to be publicly disciplined on ethical grounds by any duly constituted authority of a state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO's action here is predicated upon the practitioner's public reproval by the State Bar Court of California; such state public discipline constitutes misconduct under the USPTO regulation and can support reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific factual bases that may underlie state discipline (example: probation noncompliance; MPRE proof)
rubrics_metrics.description: State discipline may be predicated on a practitioner's failure to comply with conditions of disciplinary probation, such as failing to timely contact and schedule a meeting with a probation deputy and failing to timely submit proof of passage of the MPRE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order reproduces the State Bar Court findings as the factual predicate for the public reproval; such specific failures can be the operative misconduct supporting reciprocal action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and publication of discipline (public reprimand; Official Gazette; FOIA availability)
rubrics_metrics.description: When reciprocal discipline is imposed, the OED Director shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the specified notice of reprimand, and disciplinary decisions are made available for public review (OED FOIA Reading Room / URL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs the OED Director to publish the notice and comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; it provides the text of a Notice of Reprimand and references publication and FOIA availability for public access to disciplinary decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with other regulatory provisions (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 in connection with the discipline and publication of the reprimand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly directs the OED Director to comply with § 11.59 (publication/notice requirements) as part of the disciplinary process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of practitioner's authorization (practice authorization statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Reprimand identifies the practitioner's scope of authorization before the Office (e.g., authorized to practice in trademark and non-patent matters; not authorized to practice in patent matters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary notices may state the practitioner's current authorization status before the USPTO to clarify the domains in which the practitioner may represent clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation and signature authority for issuing orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary orders may be issued by delegated authority (e.g., Deputy General Counsel for General Law on delegated authority by the Under Secretary of Commerce for IP and Director of the USPTO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order is dated and signed by a delegated official, showing the chain of authority for issuance of disciplinary orders.
